facts.statement: The genus Myledaphus was first described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1876.
Myledaphus is an extinct genus of guitarfish.
facts.quote: Myledaphus is an extinct genus of guitarfish.

facts.statement: Fossils of Myledaphus date from 93.9 to 61.66 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Danian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Danian (93.9 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Remains found in both marine and freshwater deposits suggest Myledaphus could tolerate a range of salinity.
facts.quote: Myledaphus remains have been found both in marine and fluvial (freshwater) deposits, suggesting it could tolerate a range of salinity.

facts.statement: Myledaphus possessed blunt, polygonal teeth arranged in a pavement for crushing and grinding hard-bodied prey.
facts.quote: Myledaphus has a durophagus dentition with blunt, polygonal-shaped (hexagonal to rhombic) teeth tessellated into a pavement suited for crushing and grinding hard-bodied prey.

facts.statement: Wear on the teeth indicates Myledaphus fed on mollusks common in Late Cretaceous North American rivers.
facts.quote: Many of their teeth show wear consistent with feeding on mollusks, which were common in the rivers of North America during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Myledaphus belongs to the family Rhinobatidae.
Myledaphus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Recent research suggests Myledaphus bipartitus should be recovered as a member of Rhinopristiformes.
facts.quote: Türtscher, Jambura & Kriwet (2026) describe the skeletal anatomy of Myledaphus bipartitus, and recover it as a member of Rhinopristiformes.

rejected.statement: The genus lived during the Late Cretaceous, with possible occurrences in the Paleocene and early Eocene.
rejected.quote: It is confirmed to have lived during the Late Cretaceous, with possible occurrences in the Paleocene and early Eocene.
